paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: fixes dsh-ui table cells painting text over the next column, and wraps long
cells instead of forcing a horizontal scrollbar.
# @adamcjm/dsh-genui-bugfix
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that repairs `dsh-ui` table rendering:
- **cells no longer paint their text over the next column** — the bug where a long run of inline-cod

e chips bleeds across the column boundary;
- **long cells wrap** instead of stretching the table unt
il it needs a horizontal scrollbar.
It applies to the shipped `@changfenhuang/dsh-genui` **0.11.x** and does not wait for an upstream re
lease. Once upstream ships its own fix, this plugin stays harmless and can simply be removed.
## What it fixes
`dsh-ui` table cells default to `white-space: nowrap` (the plugin's deliberate "data columns do not
fold" voice). Meanwhile the host shell renders message bodies inside a `.markdown` subtree, and two
rules from that sheet land on `dsh-ui` output because the components render in the same subtree:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Add the plugin's own `.inlineCode { white-space: pre-wrap }` and the chip's **automatic minimum size
collapses**: the column may be sized below its own content, while the cell's `nowrap` still paints
the text unbroken — straight over the neighbouring column.
Only cells containing inline code are affected. A pure-text cell is `nowrap`, so its min-content alr
eady equals its content width and the column can never be sized below it.
Measured on a live DSH desktop page (7 tables): on 0.11.4, 4 tables and 12 cells overflowed, the wor
st single cell by **704px**.
## The two rules it injects
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The selectors use only **CSS Modules class-name prefixes** (`tableWrap`, `inlineCode`, `tdMultiline`
, `tdCode`), never the build-time hash, so they survive plugin upgrades.
Rule 2 is a **preference**. Remove that block from `lib/client.js` if you would rather keep the upst
ream behaviour of a wider table plus horizontal scrolling.
## Geometry verification
The same browser fixture, in an 801px container:
| Styles | Table width | Horizontal scroll | Cross-column bleed |

| upstream 0.11.4 (unfixed) | 1471px | yes | **4 cells, worst 306px** |
| upstream `main` (fix #282)

| 1777px | yes | none |
| **this plugin** | **799px** | **no** | **none** |
In other words: the upstream repair makes the table wider and asks you to scroll; this plugin lets t
he long content wrap, so the table fits the conversation column.
## Install
The plugin is an ordinary DSH bundle: a dependency in a profile, plus one entry in that profile's bu

### From npm
1. Add it to the profile you want it in — `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. Install it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
3. **Restart the DSH app.** The host-side plugin tree is assembled when the process starts, so a run
ning instance will not pick up a new bundle.
If pnpm refuses the freshly published version because of a minimum-release-age policy, add the packa
ge name to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in that profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
### From a local checkout
Use a `link:` path instead of the version, for example `"@adamcjm/dsh-genui-bugfix": "link:/path/to/
dsh-genui-bugfix"`, then run the same two steps.
## Verify
After a restart the renderer carries one extra stylesheet:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Visually: tables with long inline-code runs no longer print text over the next column, and their wid
th matches the conversation column instead of scrolling.
Without DSH running you can still check both halves against the loader contract:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Uninstall

1. Remove `@adamcjm/dsh-genui-bugfix` from the profile's `dependencies` and `bundles`;
2. `pnpm inst

all`;
3. restart DSH.
## Relation to the upstream fix
- Upstream `main` already fixes the overlap itself (PR #282, not yet released). Rule 1 here has the

same effect and coexists with it — both keep the chip at `white-space: pre`.
- The upstream browser
fixture cannot catch that regression: its cross-column assertion is vacuously true because the fixtu
re renders tables outside the host `.markdown` cascade. See issue #285 and PR #286.
## Layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both halves follow the shapes already used by shipped plugins:
- the **host** half is plain node ESM exporting `name` / `apply` / `inject` — the same shape as the

host half of `dsh-window-drag-probe`, which also has no host-side behaviour;
- the **client** half m
ust be the pre-bundled form DSH serves to the renderer, `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory
})`, where `factory` returns the exports carrying `apply` — the same shape as the client artifacts o
f `@changfenhuang/dsh-genui` and `dsh-boot-animation`. A plain ESM `export function apply` is **not*
* loaded, and it fails silently rather than reporting an error. This plugin has no runtime dependenc
ies, so its factory never needs `require`.
